newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech insurer Pojistovna sees 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Czech insurer Pojistovna sees 1996 loss.

text.p: Ceska Pojistovna a.s., the largest Czech insurer, on Friday said that according to preliminary results it expects to post a 5.3 billion crown loss for 1996, compared to a 412.9 million crown net profit in 1995.
Pojistovna said in a statement that the loss was caused by risky investments in the period 1992-1996, while its core business showed a 2.7 billion crowns gross profit for 1996.
"When including the influence of risky financial placements, Ceska Pojistovna will show an accounting loss which will be, at a maximum, 5.3 billion crowns," the statement said.
The statement said that for all types of insurance, Pojistovna had created reserves of some 70.1 billion crowns, which brought it in line with international standards.
Pojistovna was hit hard in 1996 by the failure of the Plzen-based bank Kreditni Banka a.s., of which the insurer was the bank's largest single shareholder.
Investigators said the failure of Kreditni was caused by dubious debt-swap deals linked to the secretive Motoinvest.
Pojistovna added in the statement that it planned to return to a profit in 1997, though it did not give any further details.
Pojistovna said insurance premiums in 1996 rose to 26.2 billion crowns from 23.5 billion in 1995, while insurance payouts were 19.1 billion, up from a previous 16.9 billion.
